To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mortalin interacts specifically with Nef's SMRs and that this interaction promotes exosomal Nef release.
the SMR peptide disrupts the Nef/mHsp70 interaction, which is necessary for Nef exosome and virus secretion.
mortalin is the first protein identified to interact with the Nef SM motif and that mortalin is required for exosome secretion of Nef.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Nef, a multifunctional accessory protein of HIV-1, in the secretion of exosomal Nef.
understanding the role of exNef in HIV pathogenesis and developing novel antiviral strategies.
the mechanism of HIV-1 Nefs secretion and its role in viral pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have identified a novel cellular host protein, mortalin, that interacts with Nef and is involved in Nef exosomal secretion, that we have shown that this protein-protein interaction is disrupted by a Nef peptide that blocks exosomal secretion, and that this Nef peptide has antiviral properties.
mortalin is a novel cellular protein involved in exNef secretion via its interaction with the Nef SMRs.
we have identified a novel cellular protein, mortalin, that is required for Nef exosomal secretion and that the Nef-mortalin interaction is disrupted by an HIV-derived peptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a cellular protein that is necessary for exosomal Nef secretion and have shown that disruption of this interaction abrogates Nef secretion and HIV release.
mortalin is an exosomal Nef-specific cellular protein, that Nef/mortaline interaction is required for exosomal Nef secretion and exNef secretion is necessary for HIV-1 virus production.
mortalin is an important host protein for Nef exosomal release and that a novel SMR-derived peptide can block exNef secretion as well as HIV-1 release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small peptide derived from the Nef protein can disrupt a host-pathogen interaction and block the secretion of exosomal Nef.
Nef's SMRs interact with mortalin, a protein that is involved in protein trafficking.
a small peptide derived from the SMR of Nef can block the secretion of both Nef and HIV-1 virions.
